learning_objectives: Explain character and relationship using simple language and an example.
Explain sequence using simple language and an example.
Explain empathy and perspective using simple language and an example.
Explain evidence-based comprehension using simple language and an example.
Apply the chapter ideas independently in an unfamiliar but age-appropriate situation.

lessons.objective: Learner can understand, explain and apply character and relationship.
teaching_sequence: Begin with an original short example connected to the learner's life.
Ask what the learner notices before giving formal explanation.
Model how to use textual clues or context.
Guide one response, then remove support.
Ask for an original example or retelling.
lessons.checkpoint: Explain character and relationship without notes and solve a new example.

flashcards.back: Define character and relationship, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define sequence, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define empathy and perspective, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define evidence-based comprehension, give an example, and explain why it matters.

interactive_activities.title: Explore character and relationship
interactive_activities.instructions: Use a safe, age-appropriate task specifically focused on character and relationship. Record what you notice, explain it, and state what you learned.

interactive_activities.title: Use it in a new situation
interactive_activities.instructions: Create a new situation where sequence is useful and explain your reasoning.

interactive_activities.title: Teach it back
interactive_activities.instructions: Teach evidence-based comprehension to a beginner in 3–5 clear steps.
